notes.title: Bugs, Updates and Fixes #1
notes.content:
Welcome Presidents!
It’s been an exciting release day! Hopefully, you managed to reach the election and even get re-elected! On the development end, we have spent the last few hours working on fixing bugs and trying to create a more balanced experience.

[b]The things we are working on:
[/b][olist]
[*] The game has an unbalanced learning curve and very high difficulty - We’re currently trying to make the game much less punishing while keeping the challenge for players who already figured out all the tricks and starts. 
[*] Map has a few bugs - Some countries were left behind in the process of assigning them neighbors. We’re fixing their relationships with others while working on the disappearing UI elements and better explanations of how to unlock certain functionalities on the Map
[*] Project trees can be defunded endlessly - We’re aware this is happening and are looking into what’s causing the problem. Hopefully, we will be able to offer solutions very quickly.
[*] The President’s private notes can jump scare you from time to time - Some laws you signed break the feature and instead of progressing, you are forced to fester with the emptiness of the President’s private notes. We’re working on this, so you can continue your playthrough without the necessity to reload the game. 
[*] Opening cutscene breaks the game - some versions of Windows have trouble with video files in Unity. We are looking into a permanent solution, but at the moment you can look into downloading and installing the Media Feature Pack from this Microsoft’s site: [url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/mediafeaturepack ]https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/mediafeaturepack [/url]
It should fix the videos and allow you to play.
[/olist]

We’re aware of many more things that need our attention, but the entire team is already busy working on solutions. 

So with these fixes currently in the works, we also have to acknowledge the mistake we made while explaining what this game is. We never meant to imply a grand strategy game, I Am Your President has always been a narrative strategy with a lot of humor and memes. As we talk more about the game and our goals with it, we will make sure to emphasise this aspect of our game much more. 

As we continue to work on the game, we hope you still enjoy playing, send us feedback. The speed with which we can find and start working on fixes is dependent on your vigilant feedback and bug reporting. 
Thank you so much for all the help and support. 
See you in the next update
[i]The Devs[/i]

notes.title: Devblog #22 - A Few Words Before Release
notes.content:
Welcome Future Presidents!
The time has come to have a little chit-chat about the last few years of development. Some of you are new here, others have been with us for years, and all of you are waiting for the next week’s release! We dug up some ancient screenshots and decided to unearth some old features that haunt us to this day. Some of them got substantial upgrades while others were banished to the shadow dimension. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/6b246e0af1f9161760737776b7ef49e669632972.png[/img]

The entire UI got a facelift, we decided to ditch the see-through brown color scheme and make the game actually pleasant to look at. Reading is a huge part of the playthrough, so better contrast and nicer colors will strain your eyes much less.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/013ecd17df58d176131236ff45964c9ffedc1206.jpg[/img]

The map has gone through more iterations than we can count. To reach this state of readability we had to change almost everything a couple of times. Countries show their names in a more readable manner and filters will help you optimize your strats. Even interactions have become more cohesive and readable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/b7c79f478cc102c5af9968bce8c4b71792f49d7c.jpg[/img]

Stats may seem the same, but a lot has changed under the hood. They have become much more predictable and easier to understand. We added helpful hints to allow so more controlled drops and rises.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/5be667455170a1ea418e8fc71089f5dcdd0c0820.png[/img]

The game's internal websites were given a more modern look. They no longer look like something straight out of the 90s. News sites will be one of the most crucial sources of knowledge when it comes to your citizens' opinions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/4268ef2a3a21f5296e66fe615a2fc131040172bf.png[/img]

The Oval Office doesn’t look like a mix of random assets anymore. We fixed the horrible lighting and installed new furniture. On top of that, we added a brand new set, which will be a part of the overall experience, so have fun in the Air Force One. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/81164dbcff4052136681892167bae74d8360d583.png[/img]

We dropped the card game, who wants to play a dumbed-down version of war with coin flip? In its place, we added new features we hope you will like. Negotiations have become much more immersive, as they are a part of the story and crisis that you will have to survive through.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/428cfa3d52c1a887793a7a1dc93d31eef5c5c154.gif[/img]

When works on I Am Your President started we were much younger and it taught us a lot. In the end, this game tested our abilities and challenged our ambitions. This has been a crazy journey for the entire team as well as all people who have supported us over those years. So we hope that you enjoy our experiment as much as you enjoyed the Prologue we released before.
Thank you for your patience and support, we could have not done this without you.
The entire Dev Team

notes.title: Devblog #21 - Things Are Moving Along
notes.content:
Welcome Future Presidents!

The past few months have been a crazy ride! On top of many tweaks in UI or mechanics and constantly balancing the game, we’ve spent countless hours playtesting. There have been larger and smaller hurtles along the way and many moments when the game and some bugs made us laugh. So let’s talk about some things we’re tweaked, changed, and balanced out. Then some funny bugs we’ve encountered and fixed.  

[b]Constant tweaks[/b]
The Map is one of the most complex elements of the game. The relations between countries other than The US and their collective approach to your presidency are a tough element to show. We created filters and color-coded systems showing specific relations. The most important element of this was changing the way we display some things on the Map. Even the smallest countries have to clearly show up, so you know who to negotiate with or wage wars against. 

Another element that we tweak, especially visually, is the Projects tab. We want every part of the screen to clearly show you how your points investments will affect your statistics and placement on the political compass. Your choices here may also affect the story, so we want everything to be very clear and intuitive.

A revamp of tutorials and the way we display them was also a big element of our work in recent months. Looking at mechanics from a perspective of a novice player can be difficult when you’re the one who made the game in the first place. Now the introduction to everything is gradual and allows the story to flow with mechanics better. Additionally, every mechanic has its separate and dedicated tutorial, which of course can be immediately skipped by more experienced players. 

[b]Balancing the game[/b]
After playtesting the game over and over again, some testers developed strategies that completely broke the game and made it impossible to lose. Every time we fix that, a new strat emerges. So we are constantly working on that problem. Number’s game is the most dangerous one in game dev. 

On top of fighting with game-breaking strategies, we are trying to find a balance between playthroughs for first-time players and returning ones. We want to make sure that the beginning explains every mechanic organically. The start of the game and how we introduce different elements have been changed multiple times so far. 

[b]Bugs we squashed![/b]
Oh dear… a lightning round of the more fun visual bugs!

[b]The Air Force One is a lie:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e5581405e532c07d8fc5c6d7ec26979394a4fd67.png[/img]

[b]Well technically... your stats can be too high...[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/40483aeb16ec5047a390d3d7cbbaa88ab1cf701c.png[/img]

[b]Snow in the Oval Office.[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/3600b93fd051b6b647780eb4bf322c647b762290.png[/img]

[b]Gigantic Babushka is NOT REAL I PROMISE…[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/43d7c4755408b6f90ba1bcaa6e8920f65e4e2c67.png[/img]

We’re constantly playtesting the game to see where we can improve performance, elements of gameplay and balance. There are also many smaller things we can’t share in detail like supplementary sound effects, new story elements and original music added to the game. While we continue to put work and effort into polishing the game to the point where we’re happy with every aspect. This unfortunately takes time, but we’re positive we can finish soonish. Let us know what’s the most exciting change we listed here. You can do that here in the comments, in our discord or on our social media.

notes.title: Devblog #20 - Tidying up
notes.content:
Future Presidents!

We are in the last stretch! There are still a few things we must do before you can sit behind the Resolute Desk and rule with iron fists. We are working on tidying up some leftover parts of the story that were a bit forgotten during development, as well as many fixes and adjustments to the gameplay. Here are a few small quality of life changes and fixes that we worked on in recent weeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/c7cf22679e2c4738f2d4a42bbe35b217901959e9.jpg[/img]

We revamped the economy surrounding Action Points. To make it more pleasant to players, Action Points will be a part of their daily income. There will be moments when some actions can change the number of points players receive. Passive income or spending on Map Events will influence your daily balance, so player choices will matter without stopping them from continuing their game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e05cbe5721c8c511cedbe8ffa86b0c9bf80d7715.png[/img]

UI changes and fixes were necessary for some parts of the game. The way the Action Points bar showed was changed for clarity. There were some problems left that the players helped us discover during playtests. We struggled with how the UI was displayed on the Map and what info was shown. It needed some tweaks and fixes, but ultimately every window should be the right size and shape to fit all data points.  

This may be the last devblog before the release as we are switching into the final stages of development. Soon we will be inviting you to the final playtests which will help us complete the last tasks we have on our agendas!
So keep your eyes out for announcements on our social media and Steam!

notes.title: Devblog #19 - Politics Are Changing and so Are We
notes.content:
Future Presidents!
An inevitable element of the long development process is the constantly changing dynamics and important events happening one after another. This is especially true when the game is rooted in American and global politics. We decided to work on updating parts of the game to make sure it’s not falling behind the current state of affairs. There are three areas of the plot and smaller details which need to be added or changed:

[olist]
[*] [b]Updating certain plot points[/b] - US politics have become more insane in recent years and we have to follow this direction. The last few years welcomed many changes in how politicians behave and conduct business. Facts became blurry and reality got kind of distorted. We want the game to reflect this while trying to avoid having to rewrite huge chunks of code and story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/3cfc78eb20135bfebbf6f86f208923be753601f1.png[/img]

[*][b] Map events [/b]- changes on the global political stage have been speeding up with many crises popping up almost daily. With the Map serving as a hub of global events, we decided to update the problems you may encounter as the President. This is where our creativity and research will shine. This is also where your help may come in handy, but more about that later. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/bafeb37d4ef2743ee9fc7ed669245e9af62caceb.png[/img]

[*] [b]Additional dialogues[/b] - conversations in the White House revolve around the current events and plans, and we want the game to reflect that. Adding new dialogues will be another way of freshening up the game, so your subordinates will talk to you about events, which you may know from the last few years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/75452998f62b2a8a4cfe5437518b36e2384e9c4d.png[/img]
[/olist]

These content changes will not influence the game’s core mechanics or the main storyline, but they will help fight the feeling of staleness. These changes are still happening and will be implemented in at least a few days. If you have any ideas on what important events from American and global politics we should add, don’t hesitate to comment here or contact us on our Discord. They can be serious, tragic or memeable, it’s up to you, we will look through them and implement the best ones.

notes.title: Devblog #18 - A Post-Festival Briefing
notes.content:
Future Presidents!
Thank you for your cooperation. Because of your relentless feedback and helpful ideas, we could find what needs to be changed or added to the game. The playtests allowed us to find and identify many problems and mistakes found in the current version of the game. When we implemented those, the demo seemed to run fine… Most of the time. This did not mean that everything was perfectly fine.

This run of the demo has brought much-needed feedback and taught us to the following:
[list]
[*] [b]the mystery of a disappearing cursor [/b]- it just went missing in various moments of the game. After sending multiple search parties and looking into the code, we found most problems that caused this. Turns out, the cursor needed a moment to itself.
[*] [b]sometimes even buying glasses does not help[/b] - we are going through a list of texts, widgets and other in-game buttons that are too small sometimes. This also touches on the importance of the correct font. We looked into it and hopefully, now everything is more readable.
[*] [b]you can read, we can write, we promise[/b] - the game is long and there is a lot of text that needs to go through major proofreading sessions. We can see the typos and we groan sometimes when we notice the dumb mistakes. 
[*][b] journalists need to calm down[/b] - the reporters were either too fast or too slow, so our presidents were left there on the podium in front of a disinterested crowd of fancy-dressed people. We hope to have calmed them down and given them a more reasonable timeframe of work. 
[*] [b]the map needs some polishing[/b] - there are a few problems with readability and sometimes it turns out that North Korea was in the EU all along. It’s news to us too, but it’s something that can easily be fixed, a few documents here and there, so we can kick them out. North Korean version of Brexit can happen. 
[/list]

We noticed ‌many people felt unsatisfied with the amount of content in the demo. Please remember that this was supposed to be a short demonstration for ‌the Steam Next Fest. After release, the game will have much more content and after that, we are planning to work on a story editor, which will allow players to change many aspects of the game.

[b]The demo is still available if you want to hop in and play yourself.[/b] 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/844980/I_Am_Your_President/

We’re still looking for feedback and ideas! So feel free to join our discord or share your thoughts on our social media!

notes.title: Devblog #17 "Projects Tab"
notes.content:
Welcome future Presidents!

Your careers are a delicate balancing act. You have to consider many elements and make sure they all work together. Your political opponents, global turmoil and moody constituents will try to throw you off balance. In the game, this will be represented by a number of statistics you have to take care of. Projects are the way to make sure they are all well balanced, while you still fulfil the political goals.

[b]Along the party lines[/b]
After the initial questionnaire, you will be given access to the project tree compatible with your party’s policies. Both Republicans and Democrats will have their own separate projects based on their policies from recent years. There are 15 major sectors in the projects tab, they have been chosen from the yearly federal spending reports. Each party has 6 sectors to choose from and develop. There are 3 additional sectors available to the president regardless of their affiliation. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/d5855342a761e482039711e3efd3452c78b0f3af.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/7f6592cd2dddbd12ecdd71621a077cf889c625ba.png[/img]

[b]Risk and reward[/b]
Each round, you can spend action points and statistics to invest in a project tree, increasing the benefits it provides each turn. After reaching maximum funding (typically 5 investment points), you unlock a specific project and are able to move to the next tier of the project tree. This decision can be made up to four times per project tree, so be careful! Once unlocked, the project provides permanent benefits - and, sometimes, permanent drawbacks. Balancing the costs and perks arriving from your project trees is how you survive the unexpected.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/2257be90bffb3cafb5f3ce104efc3f6b8d4f45c3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/87b0b49f285b779ab84fb650c7709ffd63ac7b5f.png[/img]


[b]Prepare for a crisis[/b]
When in office crises are inevitable and you have to understand how to run the White House, so you can survive until the next election cycle. Planning which sectors to fund and accumulating stats to minimize losses will help you not only from day to day but also on a larger scale. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/1e3c3cdd7c921c9d2880310f6a27f0eebc380d60.png[/img]

[b]Save yourself from game over[/b]
Unfortunately, sometimes planning alone isn’t enough and you need another option to save your skin: that is where projects come in. Defunding a project tree you’ve previously been pursuing might provide a much-needed statistics boost that allows you to survive and fight another day!

These skill trees will be your best friend in fulfilling the promises you’ve made at the beginning of your term in office. Invest wisely and make sure to plan ahead. If you have any questions about the project trees, you can ask them on our social media and in our Discord!

notes.title: Devblog #16 "The First Month of the Playtests"
notes.content:
On November 2nd we opened up the playtests for the first group of lucky players. Since then the devs have worked tirelessly to ensure that the game is becoming more and more stable and slightly less buggy.

Many updates included changes in the tutorials. Hints throughout the game became more common, so all players can easily traverse menus and explore the potential offered by the game. Some disconnected tutorials cause issues with answers in dialogues, which in turn created game blocks in a fraction of our players’ playthroughs. We’re still working on them to make sure that all replies in dialogues appear and the bug is resolved as soon as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/0f7e7c3b45286c6669b44ecc8bea00ef907d1785.png[/img]

We implemented additional content. Some of the tabs in the game were intentionally left empty, so they can be gradually filled in. Map and Projects are still being tweaked and upgraded and we added new functions to them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/579ce2adb2fa0ee74b7f4ff632e0deda099a3832.png[/img]

There were also many minor fixes, which included text formatting, quality of life changes for both the devs and players, changes in the game's balance, or nongame breakup bugs. Many blockers were dealt with and even though new ones constantly appear, they are and will be taken care of.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/7fde6a95f7c06300090f2fbdd553eba8400d036d.png[/img]

There were also updates that didn't work as expected when implemented. So previous versions were brought back. This included a project compression system, which turned out not to be as viable an option as previously thought.

We have had many questions about reporting the bugs. The most reliable way to do it is by leaving a message in our discord, we check it all the time and will be most likely to answer any questions there. You can also post your problems in the playtest forum on Steam. There is also a feedback option in the game itself.

As the updates rolled out we added more players who have been an immeasurable help to us. This will continue until we run out of players to add.

Thank you all so much for your patience and understanding! We're anxiously waiting for your feedback!
See you on Discord!

notes.title: Devblog #14 "Decisions... Decisions..."
notes.content:
As the head of state, you need to balance the will of the people with your own agenda. Your choices need to reflect the current state of affairs and take into consideration a massive number of ever-changing circumstances. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/9f45f588011d03563f6a6fcabab9d7c010d520c1.png[/img]

In previous Devblogs, we introduced the political compass and crises, and how they influence your policies. Bills you sign or ignore are your secret weapon. You choose your policy. You can make the decision to deescalate domestic problems or fan the flames on the international stage, and they sound good at the right moment. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/c938760c76dc90c7c7b4ac950fc2bc792aa2e1bd.png[/img]

We created over a hundred bills and they are scattered all over the political spectrum. They will appear on your desk and will align with your current position on the political compass. This does not mean that you have to follow wherever it takes you. You are your own boss. Just remember that decisions will help you with saving lives, creating civil unrest or maybe, just maybe, saving your face. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/1ab5fe49932e1268c426d83352d14a9453aefa9b.png[/img]

Proper bills will lessen the effects of crises on your stats. This doesn’t mean that your every decision will have a positive impact. Signing or refusing to sign a document may bring a spiral of catastrophic effects, anything from slight dent in your voter demographic to nuclear winter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/f14e8475eb3fe2faea81b642da7c52550f44f663.png[/img]

The vast number of bills will ensure that you can take your political career wherever you want. It’s just a pity you can’t write whatever bills you want, right? Unless… 

We will be posting some of the ready bills on our social media in their redacted version. For declassified bills and discussions about them, join our discord!

notes.title: Devblog #13 "The Map"
notes.content:
The world is at your feet, Mr. President.

As the commander-in-chief of the United States Armed Forces you have unlimited access to every single military operation conducted by the USA. In I Am Your President, you overwatch the world by opening its control panel, the map, where you have insight into every country’s details.

Once you open the map, you are immediately informed about the latest events on the globe. Some of them might have been triggered by you by e.g. sending out spies. Other events happen automatically, as the world never sleeps.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/1ccd213498c9559e3e4094e6c46db1e98b7921b9.png[/img]

The map offers you various options but one particular of them is what brought many players here - the nuclear attack. However, you must remember one thing - the term ‘nuclear’ here is metaphorical, as well as blunt. Once you deploy an attack of this kind, its outcome may be disastrous for your foreign politics. You’d better use it only when your Diplomacy skills are topping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/ab57eb5e5e0e2b60cd18cfaee7d096c06f071dab.png[/img]

Of course, you can do what you want. After all, it is you who owns the Gold Codes. No country shall be a challenge for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/5dd53458cd094b9e29d6ae9fb16ec53f76aebf7e.png[/img]

However, the countries allied to the one you decide to attack won’t be happy with this course of events. The more countries you make the USA fall out with, the worse your country’s opinion in the world will be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/a5370b351dfaad496585f02fc9a78ea8cfbbbc3a.png[/img]
 
Last but not least, you have to remember that the world is divided into spheres of influence. Because of that, you must be considerably cautious when planning actions on the map. That little country in Eastern Europe may not seem dangerous but the Big Bear behind it is something you should be not interested in fighting with. Not immediately, at least.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/6da171a6123cc9ab9207467562377d687b340868.png[/img]
 
People use to address the President of the United States of America as the Leader of the Free World. Well, it is up to you how you define “free” but undoubtedly you have a huge impact on the whole globe. Use it wisely.

[url=https://discord.gg/7NwNzREVrG][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e27a6aac8c58d76c5d9a76737dd5352445320563.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Devblog #12 "The Cabinet"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/91a6a282d65efbcacf54e1371d129dc6f00b4af3.png[/img]

You made it to the [b]Oval Office[/b] – congratulations, now you’re in charge and everything depends on your will.

[b]Or does it?[/b]

There is no denying that the position of the President of the United States comes with great power. However, the country you rule has been built on solid democratic foundations. The separation of powers is part of the package, hence you need to gather some heavyweights in your corner to advise you on crucial political matters.

This is what the[b] Cabinet of the United States[/b] is in [b][i]I Am Your President[/i][/b]. The Members of the Cabinet, your closest associates, are key to proper governance over the country. Every decision you make is assessed and evaluated by the Members of the Cabinet. While some of them may find the bills you sign appropriate, the others can completely disagree with your priorities, affecting their willingness to cooperate in the future. 

Nevertheless, the most important people in the Cabinet are the ones that sit in your closest proximity, around the golden square. These are the Members that directly affect your statistics, depending on their talents and your affinity with them. That is why the choices you make regarding the hierarchy of the Cabinet are crucial for your administrative effectiveness. That said, no Member is irreplaceable: you can move the Members around the table any way you like, sitting some of them around you and leaving the others on the bench – provided you have acquired someone that can take their seat!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/defd3edecd64e20f8474e9898908c4ed43da89c9.png[/img]

Speaking of which, there are also unique Cabinet Members that can be unlocked during the gameplay and placed in your Cabinet. Although not easy to acquire, these members are significantly better than their default establishment counterparts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e8dcad69c7ad5c972e588426b83a2bfaf75892fe.png[/img]

No power is given forever, and no spot in the Cabinet is life-long occupied by one person. The relations between you and your associates are fluid, so is their impact on your statistics and overall rating. Should you want to keep the office, you’d do well to closely monitor the Cabinet Members and their impression of you, as they may either make your presidency flourish or put it in the grave.

One may say: “when in White House, do as the White House residents do”... or was it “I am the White House”? For now, the chair behind the Resolute Desk is yours but making sure no one tries to kick you out if it is another thing entirely.

[url=https://discord.gg/ZjswDJbcZW][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e27a6aac8c58d76c5d9a76737dd5352445320563.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Devblog #11 "A Crisis Situation"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/7562acdbd82f2963cc8a1874f5a5da6a564a3aad.png[/img]

Sitting behind the Resolute Desk, posting Screeches, occasionally meeting international guests, and signing some insignificant bills… If only the presidency was like that all the time. Unfortunately, this job is far more stressful and complicated than you could possibly imagine!
        	
Your country is susceptible to all kinds of threats, both foreign and domestic, and it is both your highest honor and duty to protect the land and the people of the United States of America. Any number of random events could compound into an enormous crisis requiring your personal attention. Natural disasters, social unrest, riots, epidemics, and many more issues can give even the best president a run for his money.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/accd8a8646ccc386255467a578138d0a2923956c.png[/img]

A crisis can continuously bring down the statistics you worked so hard to improve. The crises can affect everything and everyone around you – your public image, your citizens’ well-being, your cabinet, and the overall condition of the country. The longer a crisis lasts, the more your ratings suffer. And if you allow for that to happen… The Oval Office may soon change its occupant. To make sure you keep your spot in the White House, you better make sure to employ proper counteractions, either by funding specific projects or making sure to never neglect the signing of appropriate legislations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/b21bba56506fd89918bc39b1f73d24d1cd180288.png[/img]

However, it is never possible to completely avoid the repercussions of a crisis. The counteractions are divided into four separate categories relating to questions ranging from enforcement of law to flexible social and economic policies - and the available legislations reinforcing each approach are dependent on the placement on the Political Compass! After all, it’s only natural for a president with anarchistic leanings to struggle with maintaining order.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/1538ee0ea1ddbf08bec0e86716e7c4147428c93a.png[/img]

The US presidency comes with great power and even greater responsibility. Events like the Wall Street Crash, the Cuban Missile Crisis, 9/11, and the Coronavirus Pandemic are mere drops in the bucket of never-ending emergencies the US have had to deal with. In this matter, your presidency will not be different from your predecessors’. And just like them, you will have to do your best to protect the USA.

[url=https://discord.gg/uQSTq23ccJ][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e27a6aac8c58d76c5d9a76737dd5352445320563.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Devblog #10 "What about... The second term?"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/b90223aa3e132ab7c1dc38104bc5e327d3e99b38.png[/img]

“Reelection ought not to be the primary preoccupation of any politician. It ought to be standing up for truth and justice.” Cornel West

From the very first day in the Oval Office, one specific matter hangs over any President’s head - the reelection. It is no different in ‘I Am Your President’.

Though fate has placed your President behind the Resolute desk and blessed him with the power that comes with the role of the leader of the Free World, it is not up to luck whether this honor stays with your President beyond the four-year mark. 

Every decision the President makes and every bill he signs affects the attitudes and opinions of the whole Nation. In ‘I Am Your President’ your voters will take into consideration whether you managed to fulfill your promises, in what ways your decisions have advanced the country, and judge how you have dealt with the crises that befell you. And the verdict? Well, you just have to wait until Election Day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/255fda4b4fa23117a144b8498f92dd428d8066f2.png[/img]

Thus, the statistics you worked so hard to improve not only affect the gameplay but also reflect the Nation’s opinion about your President. A failure to maintain the US’ position as the greatest country on Earth might prove an insurmountable obstacle on your road to reelection. Either way, one thing is for sure - every step you make is followed closely by the Nation and if you want to remain in office, you have to remind yourself of that fact each day.

A good president is one who tries to take care of everyone and everything, which might be demanding, but not impossible. The better you govern the country, the better results you may expect on Election Day. And who knows - maybe you even manage to unite the Nation and beat Ronald Reagan’s result from 1984?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/be43b147494f971597df2d0907b880c72b3bff93.png[/img]

All in all, the job might be yours for now, but your future lies in the hands of the Nation. And if you want to sit in the presidential chair a little longer, you must appeal to all kinds of voters; limiting yourself to just a few pet issues might prove to be your final mistake as President!

Do you think you have what it takes, Mr. President?

notes.title: Devblog #9 "The Political Compass"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/1737fa70b24b32ceef528b91b4e5f48c1d075ecd.png[/img]

You might be familiar with the concept of the Political Compass – a coordinate system that visually places your social and economic views between the two axes: economic (left-right, x-axis) and social (authoritarian–libertarian, y-axis). Well, this time this system will not only help you to establish your views but also define what your President’s policy will look like!
Once you start the game, your President’s views will be placed randomly somewhere in the middle grey square called ‘Mainstream Centrism’. And this is where the fun begins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/f4214f9b607e2357be230839644192d482d6410a.png[/img]

As the President, you’ll have to manage several projects around specific issues. These projects will define your presidency and also outline your President’s path on the Political Compass. The projects will reveal your political aspirations, and with every subsequent day, they will move your president towards the desired political ideology. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/8d751e28f8e06bf904766659bb63bfec698c0469.png[/img]

Of course, there’s more to that! Your President’s position on the Political Compass will have an impact on the kinds of bills he will be able to sign. Depending on the ideology you find yourself subscribing to, you’ll get the bills that will correspond to your political views. Universal Basic Income for a communist President? There you go! Complete free-market deregulation for an anarcho-capitalist President? Be my guest!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/881c9e21c15ed1f6b25ca2770f7bd750a912ca2f.png[/img]

notes.title: New year resolutions
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/2ad3cbe65f45726289f8065b0cec2b89e54ef905.png[/img]

[h1]Hello everyone! [/h1]
We hope you’ve had good Christmas holidays and are ready to bid farewell to 2020. Well, I mean… who isn’t?

This is a perfect moment to share with you what we’ve been up to these couple of weeks. That’s because – aside from the “new year, new me” shenanigans – we’ve finished gathering and analyzing all the feedback you’ve given us on IAYP: Prologue. And we’re ready to make some bold design decisions!

First and foremost:[b] we’re incredibly thankful to everybody who played our game![/b] Double points if you cared enough to share your experiences with us – both negative and positive. And while it feels great to receive praise, we’ve still got a game to finish, so we cannot afford to overlook the common criticisms, i.e. stability & optimization issues, confusing gameplay and railroading. 

Although the main game is going to immensely improve on all of those, your feedback has highlighted your expectations of IAYP. We’d really like to make IAYP unforgettable for you – not just in a singular choose-your-own-adventure type of way, but also in a more randomized and uncontrolled setting. We want our game to be a bit bolder and more unhinged than other political simulators, without dropping the charade all the way – after all, as this past decade has shown us, politics really is all about appearances!

[list]
[*][b]We’re going to make IAYP more dynamic and roguelite-ish, by, for example:[/b]
[olist]
[*]Making each playthrough denser. Less waiting, more choices!
[*]Getting rid of $ altogether and instead using the economy stat as currency
[*]Introducing some small persistent progression systems (e.g. project/tech trees start of hidden, but once researched, remain uncovered in subsequent playthroughs)
[*]Including some form of point/evaluation system at the end of each playthrough
[*]much, much more…
[/olist]
[*][b]We’re going to put more emphasis on protagonist’s political self-identification, introducing a new feature – political compass, complete with 19 political affiliations that will affect the type of legislation that the president signs on a near-daily basis![/b]
[*][b]We’re going to focus on two distinct gameplay pillars:[/b]
[olist]
[*]Largely randomized dialogues and events: the meat of the story and the spice of life!
[*]Robust secondary features to give the players (including those looking for a more serious experience) numerous opportunities for min-maxing and strategizing. This means that we’ll be interlinking all features closely and giving them enough depth to turn e.g. the map or project management into an optional mini-game
[/olist]
[*][b]We’re expanding the importance of Action Points – no need to worry about all these features right away, given the limitations![/b]
[/list]

Okay, that’s enough for now, before I get too excited… Of course, it’s not all good news: as some of you might have already been suspecting, this means that we still have some things to do, pushing back the publishing of the product a few extra months. Realistically – I do not think this could have been avoided, especially in light of the optimization issues present in the prologue. We hate to do it to you again, but we have to get our cyber playground in order, else everyone could just end up getting punked.

And meanwhile, why don’t you share your thoughts in #president-chat? Are we moving in the right direction? Or am I just rambling like a madman? Are those mutually exclusive?

Thank you for your continuous trust and support! We’ll do our best to not betray your expectations & keep you up to date with our affairs! Tons of love from the team, [b]we wish you all best of luck in 2021[/b]!

notes.title: Demo release and big status update – October
notes.content:
Dear fans, we hope you’re doing well in these strange times!

We’ve spent the last few weeks furiously debating and considering all foreseeable angles and can
finally provide you with a bit of an insight into our little IAYP project. I’ll divide this text into two
parts: raw facts (for the TL;DR people out there) and a meandering, in-depth explanation for those of
you that appreciate brutal honesty and full transparency.

[h1]SO, WHAT’S THE PLAN?[/h1]
I’ll start by addressing the elephant in the room: the final version of I Am Your President will not be
released in October – for reasons I’ll get into in the second part. [b]Instead, on the 7th, we will release a short demo available throughout the autumn edition of The Steam Game Festival.[/b] We’d love to hear
your thoughts on the features presented in the demo version – not only in terms of bugs or potential
quality-of-life improvements, but also in more general terms. Think of it as a vibe check. ;)

The demo will include the prologue’s storyline; this way we can avoid spoiling the main game, while
presenting a consistent narrative. Relive the election year as the former president: see if you manage
to fulfill political expectations and experience the events that unfold directly before the start of the
main game! And don’t get discouraged if you fail at first – there’s always a strategy or a project you
can invest in to bolster your vulnerabilities.

We’re also considering putting together an early access version of IAYP and providing those of you
that’d be interested in participating with beta keys. We still have tons of ideas we’d love to include in the final version and your dynamic feedback would help us tweak them in real time! And on that note,
we could even prepare a roadmap to give you some idea of what features we’ll be implementing
next, so let us know what you think!

Finally, as per the original plan, the prologue in its final form will be published 2-3 weeks before the
main release. Since it’s a self-contained storyline, it serves as a perfect testing ground for seeing how
adding various features impacts the gameplay.

[h1]BUT MR. GAME DESIGNER, WHY WOULD YOU DELAY THE RELEASE? WHAT DID WE DO FOR YOU TO HURT US LIKE THAT?[/h1]
To quote a famous British chef: it’s <bleep> raw!

Admittedly, it’s a bit embarrassing. We’ve got some good ideas, great ingredients and – most
importantly – amazingly supportive audience waiting for the final product! So, what went wrong?

[olist]
[*]We do not want to betray your expectations – nor the work we’ve already put into the game.
We can release the full game only once; and as much as everyone in our small team would
like to end the crunch, these final touches often make or break the gaming experience.
[*]We’d still like to work on a portion of the features, and especially the interactions between
various gameplay elements – as I’ve mentioned before: the core story and gameplay is ready,
though we’re not entirely happy with how these cogs align. IAYP needs to pull off this crazy
balancing act of being both narrative-driven and highly randomized, meaning that all the
puzzles must fit together extremely well.
[*]We’re still figuring out how pronounced certain things should be – as with any creative
project, IAYP has evolved considerably throughout its development; we’ve added hidden
stats, emotions, animations, dozens of project and tech trees and so much more. This
requires us to update or interlink the older, plainer content and figure out if we’ve missed or
overemphasized anything. Do people want more graphs? Fewer nukes? Skeletons? Memes?
Only some solid testing will tell.
[*]And lastly – on a more egotistical note – I feel personally responsible for some of the delay.
You see, I’ve been tasked with fleshing out the main plotline and went a bit crazy with it
(duh). I’ve thrown enough temper tantrums to convince my colleagues to prepare a number
of features distinct from the rest of the game. And also include some unnecessarily complex
formulas to make certain plotlines feel more organic. And also have branching out game
endings. And… well, you get my point – and know who to blame in case you find the main
plot dumb.
[/olist]

So, to sum up, we are sorry for delaying the release. At this moment, we’re a bit reluctant to suggest
a new release date – life has taught us that these things are really hard to gauge, but we’ll try to be
ultra honest and transparent with the game’s status. And, most importantly, to do our absolute best
to provide you with a great gaming experience! Anything less would be a disservice to your sustained
interest in and support of IAYP. Once again: thank you for your patience and all the kind words!

~Miłosz (Meatplanter)

Accept quests in order to get achievements, gain statistics, cards, skills or even unlock special events! Hello again, my fellow citizens!

Today we are going to learn some things about failure. Sound promising, right? Well, that’s life –   even I have to lose from time to time. So, care to join me? 

I have a lot of responsibilities to take care of – sometimes people just storm into my office and demand answers. Some crises last for several days, others can be resolved right away, but some of them are never to be resolved because of the previously chosen path… It really depends on the problem and topic but, hey, no worries. Even if you fail to help me and want to give it one more shot, it won’t get boring. The world has so many stories to be told that I can guarantee you that [b]the presidency is never exactly the same[/b] (and trust me –  I have seen a few).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/3fd67ba4c6baac8435b697a40c33b41433a85eb1.gif[/img]

Maybe after the failure you will start to wonder –  how did you do compared to other presidents? I am wondering about that too! (Just kidding, I am always doing great). After each story [b]you will get feedback[/b] –  short cut scenes will provide you with the results of your actions. Cool, right? [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/e41b1ab1d488f567ca25f4c6be1008cbfbc8d486.gif[/img]

notes.title: Devblog #5: Arrested development
notes.content:
Oh! You actually came! Welcome aboard Air Force One!

I’m afraid it’s just you and me; none of the numerous hot singles from my area showed up in the end…

I’ve always loved flying, you know? People look like ants from up here. They act like ants too, lifting their skinny fists like antennas to heavens… Towards me, their President.

When I was a kid I used to look down and examine their little routines and struggles. And from my perspective I could make all the choices that ultimately determined their livelihood: do I share a piece of candy or pierce their nest with a stick?

And you know what? Ruling a nation is no different than being a god to some anthill. You just have to map out your choices and give them a cool name, like… I don’t know, maybe:

[h2]Development Strategy[/h2]
Now take a look! Seems pretty complicated, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/6047e4d34153a75e851605a5a12703f561eeff85.png[/img]

I thought so too, which is why I asked my loyal Devs* to add cool little icons and descriptions to make it more President-friendly:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/d938556a597d2f6257a54c77f94b1eab8451f700.png[/img]

Just a quick glance can show you how many turns it will take to finish, how much it’ll cost and which sector will get affected.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/7c92449f69fc4d7c1121e1ee0363562ca8c7cc7a.png[/img]

Don’t be fooled though: these decisions matter and they certainly will affect the nation’s future! For example, I, characterized by my tremendous smartness, from the day one realized that if I invest enough in the economy, I can just focus on stirring drama on screecher instead of worrying about all the boring stuff!

Some naysayers from my cabinet keep telling me that “we’re exhausting our financial reserves” and that “even with limitless budget it’d be impossible to develop everything within just two presidential terms,” but I’m developing an AI to replace them. After all, with enough time and money everything’s possible! Look!

Spies? Check. Nukes? Check! Mechs? Check! More taxes? Check! Political blackmail? CHECK CHECK CHECK! I could go on forever!

Oof! I’m getting worked up already! But look, we’re about to land! Great timing too, now that you have the signal you can use it to connect to our Discord server: [url=https://discord.gg/g9KjvP3][b]Link[/b][/url]

Either way, we’re going to continue our conversation soon, unless some (allegedly) COMPLETELY UNFORSEEABLE TRAGEDY CUTS MY PRESIDENCY SHORT! (wink, wink)

*Thanks for feedback! ;)

notes.title: DevBlog #4 "How I met my cabinet"
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome to America, [/h1]
I am your President and I’ll be your guide. Fasten your seatbelts and brace yourself, since there is a lot to explain.

[h1]OVAL OFFICE[/h1]
Let’s start with this neat new office of mine. Lovely isn’t it? Developers made sure that it looked exactly as it should. 

Here I will be able to listen to petitioners, make some important decisions and use a lot of cool features that help me managing the country. You can sit a bit on a sofa (just take a look at those comfy cushions!), but don’t drag your feet, for we have yet much to see.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/cbe3134eaa738c91468405671c83d67c72ac264a.jpg[/img]

[h1]STORY OF MY LIFE[/h1]
I know that the picture below looks kinda odd, but hey – the result is what matters, right? And I can assure you that the result will be astonishing, since I have hired the story designers myself. So this is how they, more or less, create a plot:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/413dae9931fc4f5a77b98ccfd5228ee19a0f0564.png[/img]

Branching dialogues allow me to approach various scenarios in different ways. In the end it’s all about freedom of choice! Prepare yourself to participate in many engaging stories – would they be the ones that last for several weeks, fixed events such as midterm elections, or even the random one-day length affairs – they are all waiting for your discovery.

Remember – this is the game of consequences. Make right choices, or deal with the effects!

[h1]CABINET MEMBERS[/h1]
Hey, let’s stop by for a chat with Judy Larson, one of the many cabinet members to choose from!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32571749/cfb289443894aa02a4f1d356a861e010c65b2fb6.png[/img]

You can diversify the cabinet and pick the politicians that appeal to you. Use recommendations, get to know people or simply sink into their stories hidden between the lines. Would you guess that Judy is The Lord of the Rings fan, huh?

All cabinet members can affect your statistics, for better and for worse. They will also visit you on a daily basis, so better get used to them.
There are twenty one positions and over sixty candidates. Who will you choose to be in charge of your country? It’s all up to you. Well, and me – obviously.


[h1]DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY[/h1]
Our ride is slowly coming to an end, but don’t worry, we will pick you up again! Next time we can discuss technology development while chilling on Air Force One, how do you like that? Yeah, that sounds nice, doesn’t it? So – talk to you soon!


[h1]GAME RELEASE[/h1]

If you want to establish a direct form of contact, join me at my Discord server ([url=https://discord.gg/g9KjvP3]Discord Link[/url]). There you will be able to hear more about our plans, share your ideas and meet people with similar interests!

But what is most tempting – Discord channel members will be the first one to get to know the [b]anticipated date of the IAYP premiere[/b]! Yes, the info is coming soon – be sure not to miss it!

notes.title: DevBlog #1 "About Statistics"
notes.content:
Hey everyone,
Welcome to the first devblog of the IAYP game, where you will be able to follow how the game develops. 
In each devlog we will allow you to familiarize yourself with the existing mechanics in the game. Their development over time, recent amendments, current course of action and future changes that we plan to introduce will also be presented.

Today's topic is: Statistics.

[previewyoutube=iTrhycMx2fw;full][/previewyoutube]

Statistics are a set of indicators describing the state of our country and our relations with various social groups. 
There are 7 main types of statistics: Society, Politics, Diplomacy, Economy, Industry, Army and Money. The range of values ​​of the first six ranges from 0% to 100%. The last one, Money, can rise up and down without restrictions.

A drop to 0% of one of these statistics will mean that the next day, sad gentlemen will come for us - either an enraged crowd or an assassin. Regardless of who comes with the grudge, it will mean the end of the game. Remember, presidential candidates to make sure you have high enough numbers. Fortunately, you will get a warning about statistics that are too low in advance.

Statistics in the game are represented by a small UI bar in the upper left corner. There you will be able to check the statistics values. In addition, when you make decisions, you'll see how strongly it will affect statistics. The change can be negative or positive, but you will only learn about it after making your decision.

The UI bar can be rolled up and expanded at any time, allowing more experienced players to rely solely on their intuition.

Society, Politics and Diplomacy represent our relationship with various social groups. Industry and Economy represent condition of our state. Army represent strength of US army. Money is a budget we can spend for example on improvements. 

[b]Society [/b]- a hint about how average citizens perceive us and do they like our governments?
The Society indicator will most often change when making decisions about people. For example: the introduction of high taxes can lead to an increase in dissatisfaction, and thus a decrease in the Society index. Assistance during natural disasters can contribute to an increase in satisfaction, and thus an increase in the Society index. Take care of people's support - their votes can contribute to your re-election in the next election.

[b]Politics [/b]- the indicator represents your popularity among fat ones like other politicians, businessmen and rivals. Often their interests will be against the interests of the people, and certainly yours. However, not everyone will throw logs at your feet. Although there is no place for friendship in politics, you will be helped by politicians who have previously helped you get the majority of votes in elections. Examples of decisions that affect this indicator are: arresting political rivals for their crimes - the Politics indicator will decrease. Increasing taxes may increase this rate.

[b]Diplomacy [/b]- an indicator representing how they perceive you around the world. The value of this statistic will change depending on your decisions about the United States and the rest of the world. So you won't get popularity around the world by conquering, hindering travel from the world to your country and breaking contracts. Asking for help also contributes to the decline in this statistic, but it also works the other way around. Helping others can bring you allies, and therefore higher diplomacy. World leaders will appreciate, however, when you rule wisely, honestly and with a firm hand.

[b]Economy and Industry [/b]- determine the amount of money flowing into the state budget, as well as the state of economy and industry in the United States. You can try to help anyone in need, but it will require a strong economy or industry. Too much load can lead to their destruction and, as a result, to the collapse of the United States. You will often be able to increase the value of these statistics. In the future, these statistics can be spent on Investments / Improvements.

[b]Army [/b]- defines the strength of our army. When performing a conventional attack, we spend some value of this statistic. Leading conquests we sacrifice soldiers, but not only. It will cost us usually two statistics: Army and Money.

[b]Money [/b]- is the US budget and our funds for various purposes. From bribes to expenses after making a decision, expenditure on nuclear bombs and the army.

As you can see Statistics are one of the key elements of the game that represent the world around you. By your popularity, to the efficiency of your country. They are your means to expand your empire and the means to improve diplomatic relations.

notes.title: Changelog - November 2019
notes.content:
With the end of current month we finished some things. Here is the list:

[h1]1.0.b5 - November[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Dialogues - Added ability to express emotions for president's guests, improved guests animations
[*] Reworked UI Statistics - added fancy animations
[*] Added Atomic Thread to the World Map - Your actions against the world won’t go unnoticed. The greatest of this world are watching. Atomic Thread indicator will tell you how close you are to starting a world war - meaning Game Over. However, this will not cancel your plans to conquer (almost) the whole world. Atomic Thread indicator will decrease its value over time and through your other ingame actions such as dialogues, negotiations or social media. Gaining more and more value at diplomacy statistic will also help you to calm down other world leaders.
[*] Press Conference feature is implemented - you can answer journalist's questions. Answering or ignoring journalists will affect your statistics values and story alike. If you promise something publicly people will remember. Unless you manage to get out of it. Just like politicians in real life. 
[*] Press Conference Room Modeling - we are still waiting for a new room model and new models for journalists.
[*] Selecting the members of the Cabinet of the United States is implemented - Player is able to assign politicians to various Cabinet positions. For Example: Secretary of Defense. 
Having a dream team is a huge part of your career success. They will help you cope with difficult situations such as your decision burdening the economy of the state or unpopular decision among citizens. Unfortunately, not all of them will be useful or may be useful only on specific Cabinet positions. 
[*] Negotiations aka Card Game - Yes, we heard some of you. Yes, Card Games are bad, but there is nothing to worry about. If you are not interested in playing through this, you have a second option - Negotiations through further dialogue.

notes.title: Some hot news about I Am Your President beta :)
notes.content:
Time for some important information for everyone waiting for our game. 
I would like to start by explaining why we communicate so rarely. We are a „smoll indie dev team” and we do not have a person strictly responsible for contact with the community. That is why we often forget about this. I'm sorry on behalf of the whole team ;<.
[b]BUT[/b] If you have a really urgent question, please join our discord server. You can write to us directly there (some of us are present here every day). Then we will try to answer as soon as possible.

[url=https://discord.gg/3nPwrq3]Click here to join our discord server.[/url]


Let's move on to more interesting news.

„Soon” we want to give you access to the beta of our game. We are very excited to hear your opinions. The beta version will have limited content and will be rather short(we don't want to spoil you the most interesting events). Despite this, we will be able to catch many of our mistakes, mainly design ones;). Based on your feedback, we will be able to finally determine the exact release date. The bad news is that we probably won't be able to release the game in 2019. Creating content in the game such as events, conversations, speeches, laws, etc. is very time consuming and we want to avoid a situation where events are too repetitive. That's why we need more time. 

I would like to describe to you more precisely what this game is now. The goal of the game will be making America great again ... and survive. Seriously! During the entire presidency we will have to take care of many parameters of our country such as economy, diplomacy, industry, society etc. If at least one of these parameters drops to a critically low level then you will lose! Your every decision will influence these parameters. Really everything - every conversation, a message sent in social media, a speech given, a signed law, etc. You will have a number of options at your disposal to reach your goal. It is possible that sometimes you will have to go against yourself to survive. Politics life is not easy 😉. Even if you lose, the next game will not be the same. The events that will appear in each game will be largely random. Thanks to this, the game will gain a lot of replay value. 

[b]Tools that we want to put into your hands.[/b]
- Dialogues (...many dialogues. It will be the main way of influencing the world).
- Signing legal acts (after all you are the president).
- Creating and delivering speeches.
- Posting to social media.
- World map and some interesting options on it. ;)
- Negotiating with other leaders.
- Selecting the members of the Cabinet of the United States.
- Short-term goals.
- A press conference!
- Maybe something more? 😉

Cheers!
